snippet.title: Pepe Soup
snippet.description:
« Par la répétition, on arrive à l’excellence. » C'est la vision du chef renommé @mory_sacko_, qui insiste sur l'importance de la pratique, inspiré par une philosophie japonaise consistant à se consacrer pleinement à son art.
________

“Through repetition, we arrive at excellence.” A brief lesson from chef @mory_sacko_ on the importance of practice, inspired by a Japanese ethos of dedicating oneself to their craft.

snippet.title: Le Molangue
snippet.description:
Le Molangue, langue créée par le studio de design Yorgo&Co en collaboration avec Mory Sacko, rend hommage aux racines et aux influences du chef. Inspirée par des alphabets d'Afrique de l'ouest et de la péninsule japonaise, cette langue est aussi visuelle, reprenant des formes d'animaux, dont le héron, le hibou et le serpent, cachés dans les glyphes.
________

The Molangue language, created by design studio Yorgo&Co in collaboration with Mory Sacko, pays homage to the roots and influences of the chef. Inspired by the alphabets of both West Africa and the Japanese peninsula, it is also a visual language in which animal forms, including the heron, owl, and snake, are hidden in the glyphs.

snippet.title: Making It, Episode 02: Becoming Comfortable with the Unknown | Presented by Squarespace
snippet.description:

First, host Alex Wolf chats with Rachael Petach – the CEO of Current Cassis – about how becoming a new business owner helped her become more comfortable with the unknown.

Later in the episode, we’re bringing on Open Mike Eagle – a musician who’s critically acclaimed album Anime, Trauma and Divorce has made him an expert in facing your insecurities head on.

snippet.title: Making It, Episode 03: Breaking the Rules with Technology | Presented by Squarespace
snippet.description:
If you’re going to run a business, you have to be keeping up with all the tools of today: from the platform where you publish your website, to the social apps where you build your following. 

So how do creative people balance all these tools alongside their work?

In this episode, host Alex Wolf talks to two people who are versed in emergent technologies. First, we’ll hear from podcast host (and overall multi-hyphenate) Baratunde Thurston – who sees technology as a catalyst for creativity.

Then we’re bringing on Hanna Thomas-Uose, a consultant who has built her career helping people develop more strategic and more caring ways to relate to tech in their professional lives.

snippet.title: Making It, Episode 01: The Genesis of Ideas | Presented by Squarespace
snippet.description:
There’s a lot of emphasis out there on ‘finding’ an idea – but actually building one into reality is a practice. 

In this first episode of MAKING IT, host Alex Wolf explores where our ideas come from, and how to channel them into a creative career. 

Alex sits down with Joshua Kissi, the multi-hyphenate creative and co-founder of the lifestyle blog, Street Etiquette. Kissi has transformed Street Etiquette into a thriving agency – producing films, editorial, and creative campaigns in the same visual spirit of his original lifestyle blog.

We also hear from Brandon Stusoy, the Editor-in-Chief of the Creative Independent who has interviewed hundreds of artists about what it takes to start and sustain a creative practice.

Learn more about building the foundations for your brand via Squarespace’s MAKING IT blog: 
https://www.squarespace.com/blog/branding-101

https://www.squarespace.com/blog/guide-to-launching-an-online-business

snippet.title: The Freedom to Create at Forthave Spirits | Squarespace Presents
snippet.description:
Before opening their all-natural Brooklyn distillery, Squarespace customers Aaron Fox and Daniel de la Nuez started Forthave Spirits as a side project back in 2013.  Since launching in earnest, the duo has rolled out multiple signature spirits – Red (aperitivo), Blue (gin), Marseille (amaro), as well as periodic special bottles and a brand new coffee liquor collaboration with Cafe Integral.  All of the Forthave labels are created in-house by Aaron, who taps into his extensive background as a painter to craft colorful, striking illustrations that adorn the outside of each bottle produced.

snippet.title: Design Is Not A Luxury with Wendover Productions | Squarespace Values (Ep. 6)
snippet.description:
Design Is Not A Luxury. When you hear the word “design,” what image comes to mind? What we almost guarantee didn't pop into your head was a paperclip, or a lightbulb, or a stop sign - even though design is just as important in that tenth of a paperclip as it is in a million dollar supercar. It’s just as important in the small things as the big things, and in the modest things as the expensive things.

Everything involves design. That’s why Wendover decided to tackle one of our core values - Design Is Not A Luxury. Design is not a feature, it’s not a characteristic. It’s an essential element in any successful creative process.

Make it with Squarespace.
